sections.h2: How do you sell a house in State College, PA?
sections.html:
You list it with an agent, sell it on your own, or accept a direct purchase from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. All three end the same way, with a deed recorded in Centre County and transfer tax paid in full. The difference is how much preparation lands on you and how long the sale takes.

State College is a home rule municipality of 4.56 square miles, and it became a borough on August 29, 1896. The Penn State campus known as University Park sits partly inside the borough and partly in neighboring College Township, and that campus shapes who owns, rents and buys here more than anything else.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about State College housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 40,844 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 40,501 and the 2010 count was 42,034, so the borough has been close to flat for fifteen years. Land area is 4.56 square miles, which works out to about 8,890 people per square mile.

Only 26.1 percent of homes are owner occupied, and the median value of those owner occupied homes for 2020 to 2024 is $437,800. Median gross rent is $1,273 and median household income is $45,424. Households average 2.24 people, and just 5.7 percent of residents are under 18.

For a seller, the practical point is that a large share of the housing stock is rented. A buyer may ask early whether your house carries a rental permit or a student home license, and having those papers ready speeds up the conversation.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a sale inside State College Borough?
sections.html:
The total is 3 percent of the sale price, higher than the 2 percent that most Centre County municipalities charge. Centre County publishes a rate table by municipality, and State College Borough carries a 1.5 percent local share on top of the state and school district shares.

The county recorder will not accept a deed until the taxes due are paid. Splitting the tax equally between buyer and seller is common practice in sales agreements, though the new owner is on the hook if the amount paid is ever questioned. At the median value, an even split would cost each side $6,567 in this borough.

Some transfers are exempt, including conveyances between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings, and a transfer between ex-spouses. A deed that shows nominal consideration such as $1 needs a state Statement of Value so the Department of Revenue can review it.

sections.h2: Do rental permits and student home licenses change how a State College sale works?
sections.html:
They can, because they decide what a buyer may do with the property after closing. The borough hands rental permit administration to Centre Region Code Administration, a body that also covers Patton, Ferguson, College, Half Moon and Harris townships and Bellefonte Borough.

  • Rental Housing Permit: required for any unit lived in by someone other than the owner or the owner's immediate family. The unit must meet the International Property Maintenance Code and the Fire Prevention Code, and an imminent hazard can lead to a vacate order within 10 days and a suspended permit if it is not fixed within 90 days.
  • Student Home License: applies to one-family homes, one-family homes with an accessory apartment, and two-family dwellings occupied by more than one unrelated student. The borough adopted Ordinance 2029 for this in November 2013. An existing license can move to a new owner with an approved transfer application and a $25 fee.
  • New student homes: a first license costs $1,000, with a $50 zoning permit for the change of use and a $25 rental permit application fee. In the R-1, R-2 and R-3 zoning districts a new student home also has to meet spacing rules from existing ones, which is why an already licensed house is worth more to an investor.
  • Short-term rentals: the borough license costs $450 and lasts one year. It requires a rental housing permit, proof the applicant lives there at least eight months a year, off-street parking matching the bedrooms rented, and at least $100,000 of liability insurance.

The 2026 renewal deadline for student home licenses was October 15, and renewal runs on an annual cycle. Write to studenthomes@statecollegepa.us to confirm a license is current before you tell a buyer it transfers.

sections.h2: How does the valley setting affect a State College house?
sections.html:
The borough sits at about 1,154 feet in a mountain-ringed valley, and the weather shows up in basements, roofs and heating bills. State College has a humid continental climate with a January daily mean of 27.2 degrees and a July mean of 72.2 degrees. Annual precipitation averages 41.53 inches, with 43.8 inches of snow, and snow can fall anywhere from October to April.

The valley location also makes the area prone to frequent rain, snow and flooding. Buyers and inspectors in a place like this look hard at sump pumps, foundation moisture, gutters and the age of the furnace. If you have records of repairs or recent roof work, put them in the buyer's hands early.

sections.h2: What will buyers ask about schools, getting around and utilities?
sections.html:
Schools come first. The State College Area School District runs eight elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school for 6,712 students. Three elementary schools sit inside the borough: Coral Street, Radio Park and Easterly Parkway. Mount Nittany Middle School serves most of the borough except College Heights, and the whole district feeds State College Area High School.

  • Roads and transit: U.S. Route 322 Business and Pennsylvania Route 26 run through the borough. The Centre Area Transportation Authority operates buses to College, Ferguson and Patton townships, and State College Regional Airport has daily flights to Charlotte, Chicago, Philadelphia and Washington.
  • Commute: the mean travel time to work is 15.5 minutes, among the shortest of the four Pennsylvania places the Census compares here.
  • Utilities: West Penn Power supplies electricity, Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania supplies natural gas, the State College Borough Water Authority provides water, the University Area Joint Authority handles sewer, and borough public works collects trash and recycling.
  • Employers: a 2016 list put Penn State at 27,029 employees, Mount Nittany Medical Center at 2,365 and the school district at 1,792.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell a State College house quickly?
sections.html:
The fastest routes skip showings and repair negotiations. A traditional listing gives the widest audience, but it also brings inspection requests, buyer financing contingencies and the wait for a closing date that fits two sets of lenders.

An investor who plans to keep the house as a rental may close sooner, especially if a rental permit or student home license already exists. A direct cash purchase removes the financing step and can take the property in its current condition, though the offer will reflect repairs the buyer has to handle. Ask any buyer to put the price, closing date and who pays the 3 percent transfer tax in writing before you commit.

sections.h2: What should you check before you accept an offer?
sections.html:
• Get a copy of your deed. If you do not have one, contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff figure so you know what is left after the mortgage is cleared.
  • Decide in advance who pays the 3 percent transfer tax, and put the split in the contract.
  • Confirm whether the house has a rental housing permit, a student home license or a short-term rental license, and say so to the buyer.
  • Collect receipts for roof, furnace, drainage and plumbing work, since the valley climate puts those systems under scrutiny.
  • Check that property tax bills are paid up, because unpaid balances come out of your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax in State College really 3 percent?
faqs.a: Yes. Centre County's rate table lists State College Borough at 3.00 percent: 1.00 percent state, 1.5 percent local and 0.50 percent school district. Most other municipalities in the county total 2.00 percent. Buyers and sellers often divide it equally, but the contract decides.

faqs.q: Can a student home license pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. The borough allows an existing student home license to transfer to a new owner once a transfer application is approved and a $25 fee is paid. Email studenthomes@statecollegepa.us for the current transfer application before you advertise the license as part of the sale.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a house that is rented?
faqs.a: The permit is a condition of renting, so a rented house should hold a current Rental Housing Permit from Centre Region Code Administration. Selling does not create a separate permit step in the borough pages. Check the permit status first, because a lapsed permit can worry a buyer.

faqs.q: Who collects trash and provides water in State College?
faqs.a: Borough public works collects trash and recycling, and the State College Borough Water Authority provides water. Sewer service comes from the University Area Joint Authority. Buyers sometimes ask for these names when they set up accounts.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my deed in State College?
faqs.a: Contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds. The recorder holds the recorded deed, and the office will not accept a new deed for recording until the transfer taxes due have been paid.
